model_annotation:
This plot illustrates the performance of knowledge probing after editing with different editing methods on BioMedLM, measured by accuracy, across varying co-occurrence numbers. The x-axis represents the co-occurrence number, displayed on a logarithmic scale ranging from approximately 0 to beyond 10³, with tick marks at 0, 10¹, 10², and 10³. The y-axis represents ACC (%), displayed on a linear scale ranging from approximately 35% to 65%, with tick marks at 40, 45, 50, 55, 60, and 65.

Six lines are shown, each corresponding to a different method. The line labeled "Base" (black with plus markers, solid style) starts at approximately 43% at the lowest co-occurrence values and rises to approximately 55% at co-occurrence numbers beyond 10³. The line labeled "MEND" (purple with diamond markers) begins around 46% and increases to approximately 62% at the highest co-occurrence values. The line labeled "FT" (brown/dark red with triangle markers) starts at approximately 35% and rises to around 37%, remaining the lowest across all co-occurrence values. The line labeled "MEMIT" (red with square markers) starts near 47% and increases to approximately 60% at the highest co-occurrence numbers. The line labeled "IKE" (yellow/olive with circle markers) begins around 44% and rises to approximately 55%. The line labeled "ROME" (blue with inverted triangle markers) starts at approximately 50% at the lowest co-occurrence values and increases to approximately 65% at the highest co-occurrence numbers, generally maintaining the highest position among all methods. All lines show a generally increasing trend as the co-occurrence number increases, with steeper gains occurring between 0 and 10¹.
